name: Epaphroditus
overview: Epaphroditus was a male servant of the early church, recognized primarily as Paul's fellow worker and fellow soldier, highlighting his close partnership and shared commitment in ministry. Scripture does not specify his tribal affiliation or other personal details, focusing instead on his role alongside the Apostle Paul.
namesAndTitles: The individual is known by the proper name Epaphroditus as recorded in Philippians 2:25. Another related name, Epaphras, appears in Colossians 1:7, but no specific meanings are provided for either name in the biblical text.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for Epaphroditus beyond his association with Paul as a fellow worker and soldier. No other personal relationships are documented in the biblical record.
scriptureSignificance: Epaphroditus is significant in the New Testament for his faithful service and partnership with Paul in the advancement of the gospel. His designation as a fellow soldier emphasizes his dedication and perseverance in the spiritual battle alongside the Apostle. This highlights the importance of cooperative ministry and mutual support within the early church.
